blocks.content: kubectl cp copies files directly between your local machine and a running Pod, a genuinely useful shortcut for one-off file transfers, not a substitute for real persistent storage.
cp moves files between your local machine and a container inside a Pod, working in either direction, pulling a file out, or pushing one in.

blocks.alt: Files moved directly, in either direction, between your machine and a Pod

blocks.content: The direction is determined by which side of the command has the pod:path form, local-file pod:remote-path copies in, pod:remote-path local-file copies out, worth reading carefully since the two look similar.

blocks.alt: A syntax where the direction genuinely matters, worth reading carefully

blocks.content:
kubectl cp ./config.json my-app-7d9f8c:/app/config.json
kubectl cp my-app-7d9f8c:/app/logs/error.log ./error.log

blocks.content: 3. Not a Substitute for Real Storage
blocks.text: 3. Not a Substitute for Real Storage

blocks.content: This is worth being explicit about, cp is a one-off, manual transfer tool, it is not a mechanism for genuine, ongoing data persistence, that is exactly what the Persistent Volumes covered in the Storage module are for.

blocks.alt: A manual, one-off tool, not a replacement for real, ongoing persistent storage

blocks.content: Quickly pulling a specific log file or config out of a running Pod for local inspection, without needing to set up any kind of shared volume first, is a genuine, common, legitimate use of this command.

blocks.alt: A quick, legitimate use for occasional, manual inspection

blocks.title: Key Takeaway
points: kubectl cp copies files directly between your local machine and a Pod, in either direction, based on which side uses the pod:path syntax.
It is a manual, one-off transfer tool, not a substitute for real, ongoing persistent storage, that is what Persistent Volumes, covered in the Storage module, are for.
